notifications.docHintTitle: How push works on this dashboard
notifications.docHintDesc: Notifications API: POST /api/notifications/broadcast uses BroadcastSchema (title, body, optional data) for broadcast rules on the server. POST /api/notifications/send uses SendNotificationSchema (title, body, user_ids, type default GENERAL, optional data) for targeted users. Register devices with POST /api/accounts/devices. The bell combines live FCM with this log.

broadcast.hint: BroadcastSchema on the server: title and body are required; optional data JSON for deep links or extra keys. Audience/topic rules are defined by your backend — not the same as the “type” field on targeted send.
broadcast.dataJsonExtra: Leave empty if you do not need custom data fields. Must be a single JSON object.
broadcast.dataJsonInvalid: Extra data must be valid JSON object syntax.
broadcast.noTokensHintTitle: If you see FAILED / NO_TOKENS in the log
broadcast.noTokensHintDesc: The server had no active FCM tokens to send to (no apps registered devices, or broadcast audience has no tokens). Ensure customer/driver apps call POST /api/accounts/devices after login with a valid fcm_token (Register Device), and that Firebase matches your backend project.

errors.NO_TOKENS: No registered push tokens for this broadcast. Register devices via the API or open the app and allow notifications.

send.hint: SendNotificationSchema: targeted push for one customer. Choose type (GENERAL is the API default). Customer devices must be registered with POST /api/accounts/devices.
send.userPlaceholder: Search by name, email, phone, or ID…
send.usersLoadError: Could not load customers. You may lack permission to list users, or the API failed.
send.typeExtra: Maps to SendNotificationSchema.type (sent on every request; GENERAL matches the API default).

types.ORDER_STATUS: Order-related payload (use data JSON for order_id, etc.)
types.BROADCAST: Typed payload for targeted blast (if your server expects this type name)
